key_insight: Differential privacy in federated learning measurably degrades the quality and stability of model explanations; this work quantifies that trade-off and identifies practical mitigation strategies to retain explainability while preserving user privacy.
problem_solved: Shows how adding DP noise to federated model updates impacts XAI outputs (feature importance, explanation fidelity and stability) and provides guidance to balance privacy guarantees with interpretable, trustworthy models.
method: Empirical study: run federated experiments varying DP budgets (ε) across datasets and model families, collecting explanation metrics (stability, fidelity, sparsity).
Comparative analysis: evaluate local vs. global explanations, different aggregation strategies and model complexities to isolate where DP harms interpretability most.
Mitigation evaluation: test strategies such as calibrated/adaptive noise, feature selection, model simplification and aggregated explanation techniques to recover explanation quality.
impact: Provides ML practitioners with quantitative trade-offs and actionable recommendations for tuning DP and model design in FL deployments, enabling privacy-preserving systems that remain interpretable and auditable.
visual_elements: Privacy–explainability curve: line chart of privacy budget (ε) vs explanation fidelity/stability showing the trade-off.
Federated pipeline diagram: client-server schematic indicating where DP noise is injected and where XAI modules extract explanations.
Bar/heatmap comparison: explanation quality across models, datasets and aggregation strategies at multiple ε values.
Mitigation flowchart: steps to choose DP settings, apply feature selection or model simplification, and aggregate explanations for better interpretability.
paper_title: Towards Explainable Federated Learning: Understanding the Impact of Differential Privacy
paper_authors: Júlio Oliveira, Rodrigo Ferreira, André Riker, Glaucio H. S. Carvalho, Eirini Eleni Tsilopoulou
